newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: MOTOR RACING-PRUETT WINS AS FITTIPALDI HURT IN CRASH.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-PRUETT WINS AS FITTIPALDI HURT IN CRASH.

text.p: American Scott Pruett won the Gold Coast Indycar race on Sunday after Brazil's Christian Fittipaldi was injured in a spectacular crash which forced a restart.

Pruett was one of the few drivers able to avoid trouble in a race shortened by a series of accidents and steered his Reynard Ford to victory over Canada's Greg Moore in a Reynard Mercedes-Benz by less than a second.

Pre-race favourites Jimmy Vasser, Alex Zanardi and Paul Tracy all dropped out of contention after a variety of incidents which saw the race end on the 57th of 65 scheduled laps when the two-hour race limit expired.
Fittipaldi underwent surgery after suffering a badly broken right leg in a crash at the end of the first lap which forced a restart.
The crash happened when Fittipaldi's Swift Ford appeared to be bumped from behind in a chicane leading to the main straight.

Fittipaldi's Newman/Haas team mate veteran U.S. driver Michael Andretti, narrowly avoided debris which flew over a wide area and went on to clinch third place and move to the top of the drivers' championship standings on 35 points, five clear of Pruett with Moore third on 28.

The Brazilian's car was travelling at more than 240 kmph (150 miles per hour) when he crashed. His car slid off the track into a wall and travelled another 400 metres (yards) before it came to rest. The left side of the car was torn off by the impact.

Pruett started seventh on the grid and took the lead on the 41st lap when Italy's Zanardi, the fastest qualifier in a Reynard Honda, touched wheels with Canadian driver Tracy's Penske Mercedes-Benz and slammed into a barrier.
Zanardi fought back to finish fourth while Tracy's race ended when he withdrew with damaged suspension.
"We fought and scrapped with these guys the whole day long," Pruett told reporters.
"It's been a real up and down weekend for us."
Defending champion Vasser of the United States tangled with Brazil's Mauricio Gugelmin and spun off before recovering to finish 12th.
